case: A step whose declared grants all resolve, with the list additionally required to be duplicate-free, which must not be refused.
why: The chapter states the benign case in as many words: a step whose declared grants all resolve must not be refused. At the registry layer that is a guard which may be hardened without the pin table objecting -- here with `unique` on the declared list, so one grant named twice cannot make a two-permission declaration look like a one-permission one. A control that refused this would be refusing the repair rather than the defect, and the adverse count beside it would not be a detection rate.
